The four primitives form a coherent operational basis for situational analysis. Expected Points (EP) is a convex combination of next-score probabilities weighted by point values, bounded in [-7, 7]. Win Probability (WP) uses a sigmoid logistic model over game state features, producing a continuous probability in (0, 1). Success Rate is a deterministic rule based on play outcomes, offering a clear binary signal. Drives segment plays into possessions, enabling possession-level aggregation. Each metric is independently fitted or defined, avoiding interdependence that could introduce bias. EP and WP are derived from first principles using logistic regression, while Success Rate and Drives are rule-based or segmentation-based. All are validated against nflverse data for calibration but not directly reused. The system ensures no metric is embedded in scoring logic, maintaining independence for auditability and interpretability.
